steps.what: Verify the grave, requested service times and cemetery contact requirements
Prepare the cemetery scheduling request from the verified details
Check and send the request, then confirm opening and closing arrangements

tasks.design: Configure a request template in {OTHER}, the funeral case system, from verified details. The arranger checks and sends it through {EMAIL}, then personally confirms the cemetery's response and any conflict.
tasks.previous_blocker: The same agreed details are repeatedly assembled into cemetery requests.
tasks.enabler_now: A native template can copy explicit fields without interpreting availability.
tasks.still_hard: Cemetery capacity, correct grave reference and changed funeral times.
tasks.human_edge: Confirm the actual arrangement rather than assuming a request is a booking.
tasks.altitude: Less request assembly; cemetery coordination and responsibility remain.

evidence.claim: Native templates can assemble cemetery requests from verified fields; this proposed saving is unmeasured model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is request preparation and confirmation, excluding grave work and family consultation; no family dialogue saving is duplicated.

In s1 the arranger captures case identifier, cemetery contact, grave reference, requested date, opening and closing times, service constraints and callback details. Full capture, source checking and contact lookup remain in the 35 percent; missing details require manual clarification.

The cemetery administrator produces acceptance or an alternative only after receiving the request during s3; s3 retains the entire wait-related chasing and conversation. No structured availability feed is assumed. Changed times require a fresh checked request.
Test native templates before custom code. Additional contact maintenance is counted outside the focal denominator.
unknowns: Current request method and template reuse
research_questions: Is there enough repeated request assembly to outweigh capture and template maintenance?
